name: Swallows on dark green (1980s)
description: Ozark's last scheme: an all-white body with 'OZARK' in black bold italic capitals over the forward windows. Behind the title a broad green band runs above the windows to the tail, with a thin black line under it. Two thin lines run the whole length below the windows, green over black, meeting at the nose. On the white fin a dark green panel slanted with the fin's edges, white margins all round, carries white swallows (one small one forward, two large ones stacked aft) and 'OZARK' in small white italic capitals. Light gray engines. Worn by its DC-9s and MD-80s until the merger into TWA in October 1986.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 on N950U (MD-82, left side, 1985) with tools/photo_trace.py on shapes/MD82.json and checked on the high-resolution right-side photo of the same jet (May 1985). The bands and lines are straight on the aircraft: each is drawn at one height in meters, fitted on both photos (each calibrated on its own silhouette and window line for the camera's angle below): the green band 1.07-1.40 m above the fuselage's centerline, the black line under it 0.79-0.89 m, the lines under the windows -0.52 to -0.645 m and -0.755 to -0.87 m. Their points are where the shape's outline bends, so they stay straight from the side over the wing's fairing and run into the nose tip and the tail as the photos show. The fin's panel is set by the fin's root and the tailplane, with its sides parallel to the fin's edges (the photo's fit stretched the fin's top by about 10%). On the aircraft the green band runs on across the fin's foot to its trailing edge at the same height; here it stops just under the crown, since the fin's foot takes the crown's paint carried straight up (COORDINATES.md › The fillet) and that would carry it too high. The 1984-85 DC-9 photos show the same layout, so the DC-9s are drawn with it on the MD-80 shape. The lower lines are hidden behind the nacelle aft and are drawn on until the belly rises past them. When this scheme came in isn't dated here: it was on the jets by 1984, and the 1979 photos show the earlier one. Ozark (1950-86) never had an ICAO code, so it's keyed OZ1950. For Skyarium's ghost flights.

DC93.note: On the DC-9-30 (N983Z, sourceRefs 4) the title starts 1.8 m behind the forward door's middle, the MD-80's lettering at its own size, and the green band starts just behind it, about 10.5 m from the nose (by the door and the window pitch). Aft of that the bands keep their places against the wing root, the last window and the fin. Measured on shapes/DC93.json.
